messages:
maria: Quick proposal — automatic scheduler that falls back to cheaper/compatible model variants when the primary is saturated. Thinking capacity-based thresholds + signal routing, not just request errors.

alex: can you sketch the scheduler rules? short bullet list pls.

maria: sure — high level:
- detect "saturated" if queue length > 200 or waiting_time_p95 > 300ms for 30s window
- fallback window: prefer warm compatible variant (same arch, quantized) then cold variant in region
- reserved/dedicated customers: opt-out by default unless operator enables
- per-customer override TTL + metrics tagging for visibility

raj: minor nit: queue length threshold should be per-model-shard not global. otherwise big customers can mask small ones.

maria: yep, per-shard. good call.

tasha: what about costs? fallback to cheaper model could increase token inefficiency for some prompts. need QA/rollout hook.

maria: plan: rollout in stages with a scoring hook — only fallback when cost delta < 1.5x OR quality_score_predicted above a threshold. Also have A/B compare on a sampled subset.

kevin: we also need console UX to show why a request used variant X (reason: saturated -> shard abc -> fallback chosen). otherwise SRE will get paged.

maria: Agreed. Console additions:
- per-route timeline with events (saturation_start, fallback_applied, fallback_recovered)
- an explain panel showing decision chain and metrics snapshot
- quick toggle to disable fallback for a customer or route

raj: telemetry: we should tag all requests with fallback_reason and fallback_variant. metrics to emit: fallback_rate, fallback_latency_p50/p95, cost_multiplier, quality_regressions.

maria: adding telemetry snippet for producers:
```
metric: inference.fallback{variant="v-q4",reason="saturated",customer_id="C123"} value=1
metric: inference.fallback.latency_p95{variant="v-q4"} 420
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/fallback-scheduler -> staging (job 8842). tests: unit 42/42, e2e 8/10 (2 flaky), canary disabled.

alex: question: how does this interact with reserved capacity (Dedicated)? we must not silently steal from dedicated pools.

maria: reserved capacity bypasses fallback — those requests always go to pinned pool. But if pinned model is saturated we can fallback to a dedicated-compatible variant in the same pool only if customer allows. explicit opt-in.

tasha: policy config example (proposal):
```json
{
  "id": "saturation-fallback-v1",
  "enabled": true,
  "per_shard_thresholds": {"queue_len":200, "wait_ms_p95":300},
  "preferred_variants": ["same-arch-q4","same-arch-fp16","regional-fallback"],
  "cost_guardrail": {"max_multiplier":1.5},
  "rollout": {"percent": 10, "monitor": ["fallback_rate","quality_delta"]}
}
```

kevin: LGTM but add a hard kill switch for global incidents. Also require audit log entry whenever fallback toggled per-customer.

maria: will add kill switch + audit. Also plan to emit an incident-style alert when fallback_rate > 5% for > 5m with concurrent latency spike.

raj: test plan: unit for decision tree, a simulated traffic spike to validate per-shard isolation, and small prod canary gating by quality evals.

maria: timeline: staging canary next Tue, 1% prod for 48h after green. will share RFC doc and a small checklist.

alex: thanks — please include a short readout for support folks so they can triage.

maria: yup, will draft an internal playbook + console screenshots.

kevin: :thumbsup:. if no blockers call it approved for staging.

maria: thanks all. ping me if you want to join the design walkthrough tomorrow 3pm.
